GEOFFREY GUITON -- Internet Archive book-corpus sweep
Surface: openlibrary.org/search/inside.json
Swept 2026-09-07, under p_430.

=====================================================================
THE MECHANICAL FINDING FIRST, BECAUSE IT CORRECTS A RULE WRITTEN TODAY
=====================================================================

This morning's sweep concluded that the corpus search is "excellent for an
UNCOMMON name and useless for a common one," on the evidence that
"Kenneth J. Hollinshead" returned three clean hits while "M. G. Brooks"
returned 934. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG, AND IT COST COVERAGE.

The instrument does not phrase-match an unquoted query. It ANDs the tokens
independently across the whole book, so "Ronald Hanagan" matches any volume
containing a Ronald anywhere and a Hanagan anywhere:

    Ronald Hanagan      unquoted    total = 1,570   (all noise)
    Geoffrey Guiton     unquoted    total = 2,620   (all noise)

Hollinshead worked not because the name is uncommon as a NAME but because
both of its tokens are rare enough that a book carrying each separately is
itself rare.

QUOTE THE PHRASE AND IT WORKS EXACTLY AS WANTED:

    "Ronald Hanagan"    quoted      total = 1
    "Geoffrey Guiton"   quoted      total = 9

Nine hits, eight of them the same man, on a name that unquoted returned two
and a half thousand pages of Camus criticism and a French mayor. THE RULE IS
NOT ABOUT NAME FREQUENCY. IT IS: ALWAYS QUOTE THE PHRASE. Every unquoted
two-token name search run before this one should be re-run.

(The single "Ronald Hanagan" hit is a novel -- Sergeant Major Ronald Hanagan
in "Trial by Fire" -- and is not our man.)

=====================================================================

Query: "Guiton" "Fellowship of the West"  -- 6 hits.
Query: "Reverend Geoffrey Guiton"  -- 1 hit.

highlighter's truncation, not ours.

=====================================================================
WHAT THE OTHER INSTRUMENT SAYS, AND WHY THE TWO ARE WORTH SETTING SIDE BY SIDE
=====================================================================

ContentDM p16022coll351 (University of Minnesota's YMCA Year Book run),
searched "Guiton", 16 page hits, in the volumes for 1919-20, 1920-21,
1921-22, 1922-23, 1923-24, 1924-25, 1925-26 and 1926-27 -- EIGHT CONSECUTIVE
VOLUMES WITH NO GAP -- AND NONE LATER.

[Corrected on the spot: this paragraph first said the 1923-24 volume returned
nothing and the run was not clean. It was written from a list of volume years
in which one lookup had failed and printed "?" instead of its date. The "?"
was 1923-24, and page 46 of that very volume is quoted below. A failed lookup
is not an absent record, and reading it as one would have manufactured a gap
in an unbroken run.]

  1919-20 vol, p.380: "Montreal, North Br. Asst., Geoffrey Guiton --
      Physical, Reginald P. Thomas -- Boys, Charles G. Hewett"
      [so Hewett held the Boys' post and Guiton came in under him]

  1920-21 and 1921-22 vols: "Montreal, North Br. Physical, Reginald P. Thomas
      -- Boys, Geoffrey Guiton -- Asst. Boys, Robert E. Blake -- Asst. Boys,
      G. S. Mooney"

  1923-24 vol, p.46: "North Br., 2300 Park Ave. Chairman, A. E. Shaw --
      Secretary, W. J. Holliday ... Physical, Reginald P. Thomas -- Boys,
      Geoffrey Guiton -- Assistant, Robert Johnston"

  1926-27 vol, p.57: "East Montreal, North Br., 5550 Park Ave. ... Physical,
      Reginald P. Thomas -- Boys, Geoffrey Guiton"

  ALPHABETICAL LIST OF EMPLOYED OFFICERS, which is what settles it:
      "Guiton, Geoffrey, Montreal, Que, North, Boys', 20"
      "Guiton, Geoffrey, Montreal, North, Asst., 20"
  HIS YEAR OF ENTRY INTO ASSOCIATION WORK IS 1920, printed unchanged in every
  volume he appears in. Born 1892 (above), he was twenty-eight when he entered.

=====================================================================
WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED
=====================================================================

ESTABLISHED, from the rosters alone: a Geoffrey Guiton was on the paid staff
of the YMCA of Montreal's North Branch from 1920, as assistant and then as
Boys' Secretary, through the 1926-27 volume, and North Branch families
applied to him for Kanawana (1922 brochure, already in this project).

ESTABLISHED, from the church histories alone: a Geoffrey Guiton (1892-1947)
was an Anglican priest in Montreal who helped found the Fellowship of the
West in 1929, went to the Peace River in 1930, and later built up a school
in India as a missionary.

NOT ESTABLISHED: that these are one man. It is a join on an uncommon name in
one city with no overlap in dates -- the YMCA record stops after 1926-27 and
the church record starts in 1929, which is the right shape for a man leaving
a secretaryship for theological college, and is also the shape a coincidence
would take. NOTHING READ HERE SAYS SO.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the Montreal Diocesan Theological College's register
for the later 1920s; a 1947 obituary; or any church source naming his work
before ordination. The Storrs volumes are edited with footnotes -- the
1892-1947 dates come from one -- so the editor may well have written down
what he did before 1929. Those books are borrow-restricted here and were
not read.
